description: Deliberate improvements in the Rust build over C# 2026.10.05: answers that are meant to differ. Policy (parity/README.md, Intentional diffs): one entry per reviewed change, never a wildcard over all requests; "requests" names the requests (globs allowed inside one corpus file), "aspects" the parts that differ, and "lines" (regexes) pins what the diff says, so a different change on the same answer still fails. "reason" says why the Rust answer is better, "backlog" the group, and "reviewed" who approved it and when ("Brandon 2026-10-08"). An entry without "reviewed" is only proposed: the diff lists it as not reviewed and still counts the request as unexplained. A change a user or an app can see needs Brandon by name. Each entry also gets a row in docs/rust-migration/known-diffs.md.

lines: ^\$\.error: only in B \(Sign in with your Navidrome admin account first\.\)$
^\+\{"error":"Sign in with your Navidrome admin account first\."\}$
diffs.reason: The recovery code is for fixing settings. The C# explicit marking asked UserOf, so a recovery-code session could read, start and cancel it and write explicit marks into music files; the Rust gate refuses a recovery session on every library-file route (LIBRARY_FILE_ROUTES) with the words those routes already answered.
diffs.knownDiff: Admin sign-in: the recovery code and library files

lines: ^\$\.error: .+ != Retype the Lidarr API key for the new address\.$
^\+\{"ok":false,"error":"Retype the Lidarr API key for the new address\."\}$
diffs.reason: The C# sent the saved Lidarr key to whatever address the test named; the Rust build sends it only to the saved address, as a save already does, and asks for the key to be typed for a new one.

The C# showed a set secret as one bullet per character, up to 16, which told its length; the Rust build shows eight bullets for every set secret. These answers also list the charts plan's two settings (entry charts-settings-listed), which moves every key after GeneratedPlaylists:PopularNow two places on; those lines are pinned here too.

Undoing an ISRC retag takes the code off the file, as the undo's own answer (isrc: null) says. C# 2026.10.05 left it there: LibraryTagEdits.Set wrote the ISRC through SetText, which returns on an empty value. Fixed in the port only (Brandon, 2026-10-07); group F's LibraryTagEdits.write clears it through tag_writer_extras::set_or_clear_text (G3). Navidrome then lists the removed copy without the code (remove-copy-seen, G4 R).

A cover run resumed after a stop counts each album and song once, and goes on with only what the stop left undone. C# 2026.10.05 ran the stopped batch again and counted it again (CoverUpgrade.cs:696,744): the picked preview of 3 albums ended with albumsDone 6, songsRead 20 of 10, kept and files doubled; a replace also counted an album it had written as kept. Fixed in the port only (Brandon, 2026-10-07). The run's reason line may also differ: see cover-run-reason-cleared (the C# left its last bulk-match line there by a race).
diffs.knownDiff: Cover upgrade: a resumed run's counts

diffs.reason: The cover scan leaves the trash folder out: C# 2026.10.05 walked into /music/.octo-trash and listed a song deleted from disk in 20-library-edits as an album of its own (one more album, song and soft row, and the sorted preview shifted by one). Fixed in the port only (Brandon, 2026-10-07). Until group F's delete and put back land, this request also differs for F's sake. The albumsDone line also carries the second port fix on this answer: albums done are counted the way albums in all are (the C# ended 6 of 5; known-diffs "Cover upgrade: albums done and albums in all").

A picked cover run that matched its albums in bulk ends with no reason line, as the C# meant (its finally sets Reason = null). C# 2026.10.05 reported the bulk match's progress through Progress<string>, which runs the update later on the thread pool, so the last line ("barcodes 1 of 1 · Apple matched 1") could land after the finally and stay on the finished run; whether it did changed from run to run (17-covers-explicit/covers-resumed-done had it in one C# recording and not in another).
diffs.knownDiff: Cover upgrade: the bulk match's last line

diffs.reason: Keep as playlist works. The C# sent the playlist create as application/json; charset=utf-8, which Navidrome 0.64.2 reads as an M3U import: an empty playlist named after the time, an M3U answer the C# could not read, a 500 for the person, and another empty playlist every 30 s pass while the switch stayed on. The port sends application/json exactly, so the playlist is named after the list, holds its songs, belongs to the list's owner, and the list remembers it; a failed sync deletes what it made and backs off.

getTopChart takes chart (the overall chart, Best New Songs, Trending Songs or an Apple genre; the charts plan, Brandon 2026-10-07), so a chart's answer says which chart it is, its name and the country it was read for (null while Apple's country is not known). octoTopSongs version 2 tells an app that getTopChart takes chart and getCharts lists the country's charts (the charts plan, Brandon 2026-10-07); version 1 is still listed, so an app that knows only that one keeps working. diffs.reason: An outside song's size is the true byte count of the stream Octo relays, learned from the shim (yt-dlp's filesize, the URL's clen when that is unknown, and the bytes of a play over both), and absent until it is known. The C# native rows sent duration x bit rate as the size, an estimate that never matched the bytes; strict clients use the size to seek. Subsonic rows (search3 and the rest) gain the true size once known, so a corpus row whose stream the parity stub never sized is unchanged there. The lines need pinning against a parity run. A native row whose size is not known yet writes 0, as the native API writes an unknown number.
diffs.knownDiff: Outside songs: the true stream size

diffs.reason: Fixing duplicates keeps the best sound in the copy people marked: the copy whose id carries the most stars, ratings and plays (then playlist entries, then the oldest) keeps its id and path, and the best-sounding copy of the same format moves into it under its identity tags. Duplicates' fix meaning says so, a set in the list notes that Fix these copies picks the marked copy, and the preview's side by side view marks the copy whose sound moves in ("sound"). With the planted Harbor Lights pair (FLAC and MP3, nobody's marks) the plan itself stays the best-sound one.

diffs.reason: Plain lists (one Artist - Title a line, from a .txt file, a file whose first line names no columns, or pasted text) import as lists (import plan, Track 1), so a CSV whose header names no title or artist column says the plain list works too. A .txt file whose first line is a CSV header (12-imports/file-text-csv) is still read as a table, as C# read it. The exact A words are from the C# source; check them against the first run.

The import matcher finds a library song by ISRC first (the closest length among the songs carrying it), then by MatchKey, then among songs with the same title, the same title in Latin letters, or a credited name in common, each accepted only by SongIdentity.Same with the Owned lookup (another script and a credit written another way count, a typo does not; a name on more than 2,000 songs reads the first 2,000). Within each step the best fit by SongIdentity.Score wins before C#'s tie-breaks (length, album, lossless, bitrate). Answers that can move: a list's have and missing counts, a track's state and libraryId. A plain list is read Title - Artist when that names more of the library. Lines to be pinned from the first parity run over this branch; until then the entry is a proposal only.

Search leaves out an outside song you already own also when its key differs but both lengths are known, within 8 seconds, and SongIdentity.Same with the Owned lookup accepts it (a title in another script, a credit written another way). Library songs and outside songs are never merged among themselves. Answers can lose an outside song row and shift the later ones; a later page leaves out the same songs. Lines to be pinned from the first parity run over this branch; until then the entry is a proposal only.

Whether a hearted outside song is already owned: an ISRC in common first (the catalog song's isrc and isrcs against search3's isrc list), then C#'s MatchKey and 8 s (or the same album when a length is unknown), then, with both lengths known, SongIdentity.Same with the Owned lookup over the same search3 hits; when none is the song and the artist or title has letters outside ASCII, one more search3 for the Latin spelling, within the same scope. Album ownership's third tier reads the same way. Answers can say a song is already in the library where C# downloaded it again; stubs see one more search3 for a non-Latin song. Lines to be pinned from the first parity run over this branch; until then the entry is a proposal only.

Deezer matching counts one name inside another only when the shorter key has 6 characters or more, and two known lengths more than 8 s apart are another recording (import plan, Track 1). Answers can name another Deezer track or none. Lines to be pinned from the first parity run over this branch; until then the entry is a proposal only.

The Deezer and iTunes cover searches rank hits with one shared artist-name score (the same name, the same name in Latin letters, word-order-free similarity, whole-word containment) instead of two lowercase containment scorers (import plan, Track 1). Answers can pick another cover. Lines to be pinned from the first parity run over this branch; until then the entry is a proposal only.

Radio's owned-song check and lyrics' same-song check read a title in another script and a credit written another way (Owned); the YouTube Music radio seed is the best pick among its results (Pick, a near tie picks none); Lidarr's album pick compares artists as credits (Agree or Loose) with the album key unchanged (import plan, Track 1). Answers can list another radio song, find lyrics C# missed, or pick another Lidarr album. Lines to be pinned from the first parity run over this branch; until then the entry is a proposal only.

octo-sonic now makes every song a transition profile, which the Octo apps' Automix reads, whether Sounds alike radio is on or off. The dashboard's octo-sonic status (/api/admin/sonic) adds two fields for it: profiled, the songs with a profile of the current version, and readsSound, false while Sounds alike is off and octo-sonic only makes profiles. Every field the C# answer had is unchanged.

diffs.reason: Library health looks up every song a check found (up to 5,000, or the songs named), where C# 2026.10.05 took at most 25 a run (a16c33e; Brandon asked for uncapped lookups on 2026-10-08). So the health answer no longer carries lookupBatch, and 19-health/lookup-too-many (26 songs) starts a lookup (202) instead of the 400 "At most 25 songs at a time." That lookup is still running for the corpus's next busy-state requests, so they answer for it: lookup-slow, apply-busy, lookup-busy and undo-busy see the 26-song run (409, or the run they then start), the run reads that follow show its label, totals and lookups, and the tag-edit journal (read in 19-health and again, cumulatively, in 20-library-edits) holds the same edits in another order. The health answers' fixMeaning and duplicate-set note are the duplicates-keep-marks change on the same answers, pinned here because one entry explains one answer. Lines are the union of two Rust recordings, since the busy states depend on timing.
diffs.knownDiff: Library health: lookups without a cap

diffs.reason: A search answers with one Deezer track lookup per row and no album year; the years are looked up after the answer on the background lane and go in the cache, so a repeated search of the words shows them. A single song's answer (getSong, the native song detail) still looks its year up.
diffs.knownDiff: Search: album years after the answer

diffs.reason: getSong for an outside song carries its album year: from what is known, else one album lookup on the interactive lane waited for at most 1.5 s. C# 2026.10.05 sent no year there. Only the year is pinned.
diffs.knownDiff: getSong: outside songs carry their year

diffs.reason: octoAcquisitions version 3 tells an app that pickFoundSong takes anyway and may answer confirm, so a copy no better than the library's (or the plain song in place of a live take) is asked about and can then be replaced anyway. Versions 1 and 2 are still listed, and a pick without anyway answers as before, so older apps keep working. The other lines on these answers are other entries': octoTopSongs [1, 2] and octoImports [1, 2].

settings-keys-2026-10-09 plus Subsonic SizeFlagClients (default Amperfy): every settings answer carries the new key (listed last in config-sources, 193 rows, so it shifts no row; the saved settings.json grows 34 bytes, 7872 to 7906). One answer can be explained by one entry only, so this entry pins the combined diff line by line and supersedes settings-keys-2026-10-09.
diffs.knownDiff: Settings answers with every new key, 2026-10-11

diffs.reason: A re-pin of the dashboard files: index.html gains the Apps that hide songs without a size row (Subsonic.SizeFlagClients) on Playing songs you don't own; admin.js is the file as on main at 2026.10.11 (changed by the Find songs replace work after dashboard-files-import-pane); admin.css is unchanged. Supersedes dashboard-files-import-pane.

download with an outside id answered an empty ok envelope, which a client caching through download (Amperfy's raw cache) saved as the song. It is served exactly as stream serves it: the stub's 12,245 audio bytes, with Accept-Ranges.

The catalog songs getAlbum fills into a library album carried the catalog album's id as albumId and parent; they carry the id of the album the page was opened as, so apps that list an album's songs by albumId (Amperfy) keep them on the page.
diffs.knownDiff: Album fill-in songs filed under the opened album

diffs.reason: settings-keys-2026-10-11 plus Subsonic CoverCacheMb (default 1024): every settings answer carries the new key beside SizeFlagClients, and config-sources lists 194 rows. One answer can be explained by one entry only, so this entry pins the combined diff line by line; it supersedes settings-keys-2026-10-11.

diffs.reason: A made list's coverArt (Liked Songs, a mix, a Made for you or chart list) is its list id, then _, the cover design version and c with the song count (og..._2c6), so apps that keep covers by id fetch a redrawn cover or a new count; getCoverArt reads the list id before the _. The coverArt lines are pinned exactly; every other line on these answers is one an earlier reviewed entry already pins (liked-songs-first, cover-kind-word-any-kind, notice-glyph-covers, lists-show-current-hearts), because one answer is explained by one entry.

diffs.reason: octo_logo.png and octo_social.png draw the clean vector octopus instead of the painted one (dark fringe, noisy fill, mismatched ear pads and eyes); the logo is 41 KB instead of 1.4 MB. Pinned to the exact files.

A library cover asked for with a size is fetched from Navidrome once at 1200 px, kept in <config>/cover-cache/ and every size is cut from that copy in Octo (Catmull-Rom, JPEG q85), so the bytes of a small size differ from Navidrome's own resize. Pinned to the exact picture.
